# **1\. Project overview** {#1.-project-overview}

## **1.1 Project Title** {#1.1-project-title}

AutoRestTest: An AI-Powered Platform for Automated REST API Testing 

## **1.2 Problem Statement** {#1.2-problem-statement}

As modern web services increasingly rely on REST APIs, ensuring their correctness is critical. As APIs grow in size and complexity, testing them becomes progressively harder because of large input spaces, interdependent operations, and the need for valid request sequences. Traditional automated testing tools often fail to explore these dependencies effectively, leading to low coverage, missed edge cases, and weak fault detection, while manual testing is time-consuming, repetitive, error-prone, and unable to scale with continuous development. Recent research such as AutoRestTest \[1\] shows that dependency-aware, reinforcement-learning and LLM-powered test generation can substantially improve coverage and fault detection for REST APIs. At the same time, development teams need a centralized, collaborative environment in which specifications, test suites, execution results, and reports can be stored, shared, and reused over time. Existing solutions rarely combine an intelligent testing engine with such a platform, and this gap is the problem this project addresses.

## **1.3 Objectives** {#1.3-objectives}

The main objectives of this project are as follows:

* To design and develop an AI-powered, collaborative SaaS platform for automated REST API testing, accessible through a centralized web dashboard.  
* To integrate an intelligent testing engine that uses dependency-aware, reinforcement-learning and LLM-based request generation, inspired by the AutoRestTest \[1\] approach, to maximize coverage and fault detection.  
* To allow users to upload OpenAPI specifications, or generate them with AI-assisted analysis, and to extract their endpoints automatically.  
* To automatically generate, save, and reuse test suites for each project.  
* To provide one-click, asynchronous test execution with real-time status updates and persistent execution history.  
* To present clear results and analytics, including status-code distribution, coverage, and server failures, together with LLM-based failure explanations and exportable PDF/CSV reports.  
* To enable secure team collaboration through project sharing and role-based access control.

## **1.4 Scope** {#1.4-scope}

The scope of this project defines the boundaries of the platform and the extent of the functionality it delivers. AutoRestTest is a web-based SaaS application for the functional testing of RESTful web services described by OpenAPI 3.0 specifications. Within this boundary it supports the complete testing workflow through a single centralized dashboard, from user and project management to specification handling, AI-driven test generation and execution, result analysis and reporting, and multi-user collaboration, so that development teams can automate REST API testing and reduce manual effort.

Certain areas are intentionally outside the scope of this project. The platform targets REST APIs only and does not address SOAP, GraphQL, or gRPC services, nor specification formats other than OpenAPI 3.0. It focuses on functional and fault-detection testing rather than load, stress, or performance testing, and it does not modify, deploy, or manage the systems under test. The platform further assumes that the target API is reachable over the network and that any credentials required to access protected endpoints are provided by the user.

## **1.5 Deliverables** {#1.5-deliverables}

The main deliverables of this project are as follows:

* A deployed web application (frontend and backend) that provides the AutoRestTest platform through a centralized, browser-based dashboard.  
* An AI-powered testing engine, deployed as an independent service, that performs dependency-aware, reinforcement-learning and LLM-based test generation and execution.  
* A PostgreSQL database implementing the platform's data model for users, projects, specifications, test suites, executions, results, and collaboration.  
* A complete, documented source-code repository covering the frontend, backend, and testing engine.  
* This technical report, documenting the project's overview, requirements, system and data models, AI engineering design, preliminary test plan and timeline.

# **2\. Requirements Analysis** {#2.-requirements-analysis}

## **2.1 Quality Function Deployment** {#2.1-quality-function-deployment}

### **2.1.1 Normal Requirements** {#2.1.1-normal-requirements}

Explicitly requested core features; user satisfaction is proportional to how well they are met.

#### **Functional Requirements** {#functional-requirements}

- [ ] **FR-N1 — User Authentication:** register, log in, and maintain secure sessions.  
- [ ] **FR-N2 — Project Management:** create, open, rename, and delete API testing projects from a central dashboard.  
- [ ] **FR-N3 — Specification Upload:** upload an OpenAPI 3.0 file; the system parses it and lists the extracted endpoints.  
- [ ] **FR-N4 — Test Execution:** run automated requests against the target API from a specification and collect the responses.  
- [ ] **FR-N5 — Result Viewing:** view each run's outcome per endpoint (method, request, response, status code, pass/fail).  
- [ ] **FR-N6 — Completion Notifications:** notify the user when a run completes, fails, or errors.

#### **Non-Functional Requirements** {#non-functional-requirements}

- [ ] **NFR-N1 — Usability:** the whole workflow is driven from one intuitive web dashboard, usable without special training.  
- [ ] **NFR-N2 — Responsiveness:** routine interactions (dashboard, navigation) load within a couple of seconds.

### **2.1.2 Expected Requirements** {#2.1.2-expected-requirements}

Implicitly assumed; their absence causes dissatisfaction even though users rarely ask for them by name.

#### **Functional Requirements** {#functional-requirements-1}

- [ ] **FR-E1 — Automatic Test Suite Generation:** automatically generate a comprehensive, dependency-aware suite of test cases from the specification.  
- [ ] **FR-E2 — Save & Reuse Suites:** persist named test suites for re-execution without reconfiguration.  
- [ ] **FR-E3 — Execution History:** keep every past run with its timestamp and outcome for later review.  
- [ ] **FR-E4 — Reports & Analytics:** per-run summary of HTTP status-code distribution, coverage, and server failures.  
- [ ] **FR-E5 — Export Reports:** download a run's results as PDF or CSV.  
- [ ] **FR-E6 — Team Collaboration:** invite members to a project and assign roles (admin, tester, viewer).

#### **Non-Functional Requirements** {#non-functional-requirements-1}

- [ ] **NFR-E1 — Security & Data Privacy:** passwords hashed, routes JWT-protected, and each user's and project's data isolated via role-based access control.  
- [ ] **NFR-E2 — Reliability:** long-running executions run asynchronously without blocking the UI and report status accurately.  
- [ ] **NFR-E3 — Data Persistence:** specifications, suites, runs, and results are stored durably and remain available across sessions.

### **2.1.3 Exciting Requirements** {#2.1.3-exciting-requirements}

Delighters beyond expectation; their absence isn't penalised, but their presence differentiates the platform. 

#### **Functional Requirements** {#functional-requirements-2}

- [ ] **FR-X1 — One-Click End-to-End Testing:** a single action runs the entire pipeline — read spec, generate tests, execute, and produce a report.  
- [ ] **FR-X2 — AI Failure Explanation:** LLM-generated, plain-language explanation of what caused a failure and which request triggered it.  
- [ ] **FR-X3 — AI Specification Generation:** automatically generate an OpenAPI specification from uploaded source code.

#### **Non-Functional Requirements** {#non-functional-requirements-2}

- [ ] **NFR-X1 — Extensibility:** the AI testing engine is deployed as an independent service, so its generation strategy can evolve without changing the web platform.

## **2.2 Stakeholders** {#2.2-stakeholders}

The key stakeholders of the platform and their interests are summarised below:

* API Developer: Uploads specifications and runs tests to catch defects in their REST APIs early.  
* QA Engineer / Tester: Generates and executes test suites and reviews results and failure explanations.  
* Team Lead / Project Manager: Creates projects, invites members, assigns roles, and tracks testing progress.  
* Viewer (Client / Stakeholder): Reviews reports and analytics without modifying tests.

## **2.3 Usage Scenario** {#2.3-usage-scenario}

### **2.3.1 Authentication System** {#2.3.1-authentication-system}

The system will have an authentication system with two options: sign up for new users and log in for users who already have an account.

**User Sign Up**  
A new user will begin registration by visiting the platform's sign-up page and clicking the Create Account button. The user will need to provide a valid email address, a username, and a password. The system will validate the uniqueness of the username and email and the format of the email address.

**User Login**  
Already registered users can log in by providing their email address and password on the login page. The system will maintain user sessions securely, allowing users to remain logged in without having to authenticate repeatedly. Users will also have the option to keep their login details saved for quicker access in future sessions.

### **2.3.2 Project Management** {#2.3.2-project-management}

Once logged in, users will be taken to the main dashboard where all their projects are displayed. The system will allow users to create, manage, and organise multiple API testing projects from a single centralised interface.

**Create Project**  
A user can create a new project by clicking the New Project button on the dashboard. The user will provide a project name and an optional description. Once created, the project will appear on the dashboard and the user will be taken to the project workspace where they can begin setting up their testing environment.

**Manage Projects**  
The dashboard will display all projects belonging to the user along with their names, creation dates, and last activity. Users can open, rename, or delete any project from the dashboard. Users can add multiple API endpoints inside a project. Deleting a project will remove all associated specifications, test suites, and results permanently, following a confirmation prompt from the system.

### **2.3.3 API Specification Management** {#2.3.3-api-specification-management}

Before testing can begin, users need to define the API they want to test. Each project may have an API specification. The system will provide two ways to do this: uploading an existing specification file or generating one automatically from source code.

**Upload OpenAPI Specification**  
Users can upload an OpenAPI specification file in .yaml format directly into their project. The system will parse and validate the uploaded file and display the list of detected API endpoints and operations, making them available for test generation. If the file contains errors or is not a valid specification, the system will notify the user with a description of the problem.

**Automated API Specification Generation**  
For users who do not have an existing specification file, the system will provide an option to generate one automatically. The user can upload their API source code files and the system will analyse them to produce a valid OpenAPI specification. The generated specification will be displayed for review before the user proceeds, and it can be used as the basis for testing in the same way as a manually uploaded file.

### **2.3.4 Test Suite Management** {#2.3.4-test-suite-management}

Once an API specification is available within the project, the system will allow users to generate, save, and reuse test suites for repeated testing.

**Automatic Test Suite Generation**  
After a specification is uploaded or generated, the system will automatically produce a comprehensive set of test cases covering the detected API endpoints and operations. The generated test suite will be displayed to the user showing each test case, its target endpoint, and the HTTP method that will be used. Users are not required to write or configure any test cases manually.

**Save and Reuse Test Suites**  
The test suite will be saved for future use. Saved test suites will appear in the project's Test Suites section and can be re-executed at any time without regenerating or reconfiguring them. This is particularly useful for regression testing, where the same suite needs to be run repeatedly after API changes.

### **2.3.5 Test Execution** {#2.3.5-test-execution}

When a test suite is executed, the system will send automated requests to the target API, collect the responses, and track the progress in real time.

**One-Click API Testing**  
The system will provide a single Run button that, when clicked, triggers the entire testing pipeline automatically. The system will read the active specification, generate test cases, execute all tests against the target API, and produce a full report — all without requiring any additional input from the user. This allows a team to run a complete API test in a single action.

**Running Tests**  
Users can initiate a test run by selecting a test suite and clicking the Run button. The system will display a live progress indicator showing which endpoints are currently being tested and how many have been completed. Users can monitor the execution as it progresses without needing to refresh the page.

**Test Alerts and Notifications**  
Once a test run is complete, the system will send the user a notification confirming completion along with a brief summary of the outcome. If the run encounters a failure — such as the target API being unreachable, an unexpected server error, or a system-level issue during execution — the user will be notified immediately with a description of what went wrong.

### **2.3.6 Test Results and Reports** {#2.3.6-test-results-and-reports}

After each test run, the system will store the results and provide detailed reporting and analysis options for the user to review.

**Viewing Test Results**  
Users can open any completed test run to see a full breakdown of the results. The results page will show each endpoint that was tested, the HTTP method used, the response received, and whether the test passed or failed. Users can filter the results by endpoint, response status, or HTTP response code to focus on specific areas of interest. In addition, the system records every individual request the engine sent during the run, so users can inspect the exact request and response captured for each call.

**Test Reports and Analytics**  
The system will generate a summary report for each completed test run showing the distribution of HTTP response codes received across all tested endpoints, any server-side failures that were detected, and the proportion of the API's endpoints that were covered during the run. This gives the team a complete picture of how the API performed.

**Test Failure Explanation**  
When a server-side failure or unexpected response is detected, the system will provide a plain-language explanation describing which request triggered the failure, what response was received, and what the likely cause may be. This reduces the time users spend investigating and diagnosing issues after a test run.

**Test Execution History**  
The system will maintain a complete history of all test runs for each project. Users can access the history from the project workspace and see a list of past executions with their timestamps, the test suite used, and a summary of outcomes. Any past run can be opened to review its full results in the same way as a recent run.

**Export Test Reports**  
Users can download the results and report of any completed test run in standard formats such as PDF or CSV. The exported file will contain the full results breakdown, the analytics summary, and the details of any detected failures, allowing users to share test outcomes with stakeholders or include them in project documentation.

### **2.3.7 Team Collaboration** {#2.3.7-team-collaboration}

The system will allow multiple users to collaborate within a shared project. The project owner can invite team members and assign them roles to control what each member can see and do within the project.

**Inviting Team Members**  
The project owner or an admin can invite other users to join the project by entering their email address. The invited user will receive an invitation with a link to accept it. Once accepted, the user will be added to the project and it will appear on their dashboard.

**Role Management**  
Each team member is assigned a role that determines their level of access. An admin can manage project settings, invite or remove members, and execute test runs. A tester can upload specifications, generate test suites, and run tests. A viewer can only see test results and reports without making any changes to the project. The project owner can update a member's role or remove them from the project at any time.

# **4\. Data Modeling** {#4.-data-modeling}

Database modeling describes how the platform's persistent data is structured and related. AutoRestTest uses a relational schema on **PostgreSQL**, accessed through the **Prisma** ORM. The model comprises nine entities and four enumerated types.

## **4.1 ER Diagram**  {#4.1-er-diagram}

Entity Relationships:

* A **User** can own many **Projects**.  
* A **User** can belong to many **Projects** through **ProjectMember**, a many-to-many association that carries the member's role (each row pairs one user with one project).  
* A **Project** can have many **ProjectInvitations**, and each invitation is sent by one **User**.  
* A **Project** has at most one **ApiSpecification**.  
* A **Project** contains many **Endpoints**.  
* A **Project** can have many **TestSuites**, and each **TestSuite** is triggered by one **User**.  
* A **TestSuite** produces many **TestCases**, and each **TestCase** tests one **Endpoint**.  
* A **TestSuite** captures many **RequestLogs**, and each **RequestLog** maps to at most one **Endpoint**.

![][image17]

*Figure 17: Entity Relationship Diagram* 

## 

## **4.2 Database schema** {#4.2-database-schema}

**Table: Database schemas.** PK \= primary key, FK \= foreign key, → \= references. All identifiers are UUID strings.

| Schema | Attribute | Type |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **User** | id (PK) | TEXT (UUID) |
|  | username | TEXT, UNIQUE |
|  | email | TEXT, UNIQUE |
|  | password | TEXT (bcrypt hash) |
|  | createdAt | TIMESTAMP |
|  | updatedAt | TIMESTAMP |
| **Project** | id (PK) | TEXT (UUID) |
|  | name | TEXT |
|  | description | TEXT (nullable) |
|  | ownerId (FK) | TEXT → User |
|  | createdAt | TIMESTAMP |
|  | updatedAt | TIMESTAMP |
| **ProjectMember** | id (PK) | TEXT (UUID) |
|  | projectId (FK) | TEXT → Project |
|  | userId (FK) | TEXT → User |
|  | role | ENUM(admin, tester, viewer) |
|  | joinedAt | TIMESTAMP |
| **ProjectInvitation** | id (PK) | TEXT (UUID) |
|  | projectId (FK) | TEXT → Project |
|  | email | TEXT |
|  | role | ENUM(admin, tester, viewer) |
|  | token | TEXT, UNIQUE |
|  | status | ENUM(pending, accepted, declined, expired) |
|  | invitedById (FK) | TEXT → User |
|  | expiresAt | TIMESTAMP |
|  | createdAt | TIMESTAMP |
| **ApiSpecification** | id (PK) | TEXT (UUID) |
|  | projectId (FK) | TEXT → Project, UNIQUE |
|  | fileName | TEXT |
|  | fileContent | TEXT (raw OpenAPI 3.0) |
|  | generatedByAI | BOOLEAN |
|  | uploadedAt | TIMESTAMP |
| **Endpoint** | id (PK) | TEXT (UUID) |
|  | projectId (FK) | TEXT → Project |
|  | path | TEXT |
|  | method | ENUM(GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) |
|  | description | TEXT (nullable) |
|  | addedManually | BOOLEAN |
|  | createdAt | TIMESTAMP |
| **TestSuite** | id (PK) | TEXT (UUID) |
|  | projectId (FK) | TEXT → Project |
|  | name | TEXT (nullable) |
|  | status | ENUM(pending, running, completed, failed) |
|  | jobId | TEXT (nullable) |
|  | targetUrl | TEXT |
|  | timeBudget | INTEGER |
|  | mutationRate | DOUBLE PRECISION |
|  | totalEndpoints | INTEGER |
|  | coveredEndpoints | INTEGER |
|  | totalTestCases | INTEGER |
|  | passedTestCases | INTEGER |
|  | failedTestCases | INTEGER |
|  | triggeredById (FK) | TEXT → User |
|  | startedAt | TIMESTAMP (nullable) |
|  | completedAt | TIMESTAMP (nullable) |
|  | createdAt | TIMESTAMP |
| **TestCase** | id (PK) | TEXT (UUID) |

# **5\. AI Engineering**  {#5.-ai-engineering}

# **6\. Preliminary Test Plan** {#6.-preliminary-test-plan}

## **6.1 High-Level Description of Testing Goals** {#6.1-high-level-description-of-testing-goals}

The testing goals for this platform are represented below from a high level:

* To verify that AutoRestTest meets its most important functional and non-functional requirements.  
* To ensure that users can securely register, authenticate, and access only the projects they are authorized for.  
* To confirm that uploaded OpenAPI specifications are parsed correctly and that endpoints are extracted accurately.  
* To ensure that the AI testing engine generates valid requests and executes test suites reliably.  
* To confirm that long-running test executions run asynchronously without blocking the user while reporting status reliably.  
* To verify that test results, analytics, and LLM-based failure explanations are accurate and clearly presented.  
* To confirm that reports can be exported (PDF/CSV) and that test-execution history is preserved.  
* To guarantee that team collaboration and role-based access control work correctly and securely.

## **6.2 Test Cases** {#6.2-test-cases}

The test cases for the testing of this platform are documented below:

| Test Case Id | T1 |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Title** | User Registration and Login |
| **Test Scenario** | \- Register a new account with a valid name, email, and password. \- Log in using the same credentials, then retry with a wrong password. |
| **Expected Outcome** | The account is created with a securely hashed password, a JWT token is issued on valid login and the user reaches the dashboard, while invalid credentials are rejected. |

                                                      *Table – 1: Test Plan – 1*

| Test Case Id | T2 |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Title** | Project Creation and Access Control |
| **Test Scenario** | \- Create a new project as its owner. \- Attempt to open the same project from an unrelated account. |
| **Expected Outcome** | The project is created with the creator as admin and appears on the owner's dashboard, while the unauthorized account is denied access. |

                                                       *Table – 2: Test Plan – 2*

| Test Case Id | T3 |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Title** | OpenAPI Specification Upload and Parsing |
| **Test Scenario** | \- Upload a valid OpenAPI 3.0 specification to a project. \- Then upload a malformed specification file. |
| **Expected Outcome** | The valid specification is stored and its endpoints (path and method) are extracted and listed correctly, while the malformed file is rejected with a clear error message. |

                                                        *Table – 3: Test Plan – 3*

| Test Case Id | T4 |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Title** | Automatic Test Suite Generation |
| **Test Scenario** | \- Trigger automatic test-suite generation for a parsed specification. |
| **Expected Outcome** | A test suite containing test cases that cover the specification's operations is generated and saved so it can be reused later. |

                                                        *Table – 4: Test Plan – 4*

| Test Case Id | T5 |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Title** | One-Click Test Execution |
| **Test Scenario** | \- Run a generated test suite with a single action. \- Observe the suite status while it runs. |
| **Expected Outcome** | The backend creates an asynchronous job, the suite status transitions from pending to running to completed, and the interface stays responsive throughout. |

                                                           *Table – 5: Test Plan – 5*

| Test Case Id | T6 |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Title** | Viewing and Filtering Test Results |
| **Test Scenario** | \- Open a completed test run. \- Filter the results by endpoint, status, and response code. |
| **Expected Outcome** | The results (endpoints, methods, responses, and pass/fail outcomes) are displayed, and each filter returns the correct subset of test cases. |

                                                             *Table – 6: Test Plan – 6*

| Test Case Id | T7 |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Title** | Captured Request and Response Inspection |
| **Test Scenario** | \- Select a test case from a completed run and inspect its captured request and response. |
| **Expected Outcome** | The full request (method, URL, headers, and body) and the response (status code and body) are shown exactly as they were logged. |

                                                                *Table – 7: Test Plan – 7*

| Test Case Id | T8 |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Title** | Analytics and LLM Failure Explanation |
| **Test Scenario** | \- View the analytics for a run (response-code distribution, coverage, and server failures). \- Request an explanation for a failed test case. |
| **Expected Outcome** | The analytics accurately reflect the run and the LLM produces a relevant, understandable explanation for the failure. |

                                                              *Table – 8: Test Plan – 8*

| Test Case Id | T9 |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Title** | Exporting Test Reports |
| **Test Scenario** | \- Export a completed run's report as PDF and as CSV. |
| **Expected Outcome** | Both files download successfully and contain the run's results accurately. |

                                                         *Table – 9: Test Plan – 9*

| Test Case Id | T10 |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Title** | Team Collaboration and Role Management |
| **Test Scenario** | \- Invite a user by email with an assigned role (tester or viewer). \- Accept the invitation and attempt an action beyond the assigned role. |
| **Expected Outcome** | An invitation with a unique token is created, the invited user becomes a member with the assigned role on acceptance, and actions outside that role are restricted. |
